list.heading: Databases
list.subtitle: MySQL databases and their dedicated users.
list.prefixNote: Every database and user carries the owning account's name as a prefix. The names below are exactly what MySQL holds — use them as they are.
list.emptyDescription: Create the first database above. Its password is shown once, when it is created.
list.confirmResetPassword: Set a new password? The current one stops working immediately.
list.confirmDrop: Drop this database? Its tables and its user go with it, and nothing here can bring them back.

form.hint: Lowercase letters and digits only. The account's name is added in front of both.

errors.accountRequired: Choose the account that will own the database.
errors.nameInvalid: Use lowercase letters and digits only, up to 30 characters.
errors.dbUserNameInvalid: Use lowercase letters and digits only, up to 30 characters.

credential.title: Database password
credential.warning: This password is shown once. Nothing keeps a copy of it — not this panel, not the server — so it cannot be shown again. Copy it before you close this.
credential.resetHint: If it is lost, reset the password from the list. That is the only way back — there is nothing to recover.

grantRepair.heading: Grant repair
grantRepair.subtitle: What this server's database grants hold, and what a repair would narrow.
grantRepair.adminNote: Administrators only. The list spans every account on this server, so it names databases and users that belong to other customers.
grantRepair.notDisclosedDescription: This page reads the grants of every account on the server at once, so only an administrator may open it. It says nothing about your own databases either way — ask your provider if you need it checked.

census.heading: What the server holds
census.sumNote: The four figures add up to the grants read: every row was put in exactly one of them, so this is the whole grant table and not a selection from it.

changed.subtitle: Grants this panel issued whose stored name had stopped naming one database.
changed.emptyDescription: Every grant this panel issued on this server already names exactly one database.
changed.alsoMatchedNone: No other database on the server matches it right now.
changed.exposureNote: The databases listed are ones the credential could have read and written while its grant was wide. That is what it could reach, not what it did. An empty list does not clear a row either: a matching database may have been created and dropped in between, and the name is matched when a client connects, not when this page is read.
changed.notCleanNote: A repair closes the reach from now on. It does not establish whether anyone used it, and it does not make this server clean of what happened before. Only your database server's query log can answer that, and it is off unless you turned it on.

refused.heading: Left exactly as found
refused.subtitle: Rows this panel will not touch, with what each one needs from you.
refused.emptyDescription: Every row on this server was either already correct or one this panel could safely narrow.
refused.notYoursNote: A row is left alone precisely because this panel did not create it, so the names above are frequently somebody else's — another customer's database, or a credential you or your database administrator made by hand.

action.heading: Run the repair
action.subtitle: Only ever on the list above, and only while it still describes this server.
action.readReportFirst: The repair is offered on a fresh reading of the server's grants. Read them again to get it back.
action.nothingToDo: There is nothing for the repair to narrow on this server.

confirm.title: Narrow the grants listed
confirm.question: This rewrites live database access for {grants} on this server, one customer's application at a time. Nothing else on the server is touched, and rows the panel refused stay exactly as they are.
